title: Polymer‐Directed Crystal Growth Regulation: Template‐Free Synthesis of Mesoporous Single‐Crystalline Mn 2 OBO 3
abstract: ABSTRACT Transition metal borates are attractive anode candidates for lithium‐ion batteries (LIBs) because of their high specific capacity and environmental benignity; however, their structural collapse induced by large volume changes during cycling leads to rapid capacity degradation. In this study, we report a polymer‐directed crystal growth regulation strategy that enables the template‐free synthesis of mesoporous single‐crystalline Mn 2 OBO 3 (MSC Mn 2 OBO 3 ). Polyethyleneimine (PEI) acts as a bifunctional regulator, coordinating Mn 2+ ions and hydrogen bonding with borate ions to modulate hydrolysis and condensation, thereby yielding a hybrid precursor. Subsequent hydrothermal treatment yields single‐crystalline MnBO 2 OH nanobelts, which are converted by calcination into MSC Mn 2 OBO 3 . As an anode active material for lithium‐ion batteries, MSC Mn 2 OBO 3 delivers a reversible capacity of 1440 mAh g −1 at 0.2 A g −1 , more than twice that of bulk Mn 2 OBO 3 . Notably, this polymer‐directed strategy is readily extendable to doped MSC Mn 2 OBO 3 (e.g., Fe, V, and Mg), providing a versatile platform for the design of porous single‐crystalline materials for energy storage.

title: Interfacial Electric Field Dynamically Confined Enzyme Self-Adaptation in Covalent Organic Framework Heterojunctions for Photoenzymatic Catalysis
abstract: Abstract Artificial photoenzymatic synthesis systems based on 1,4-NADH-dependent enzymes are challenged by unclear interfacial interactions and limited stability. Inspired by the ordered assembly and Z-scheme electron transfer mechanism in natural photosynthesis, we constructed an enzyme self-adaptive covalent organic frameworks (COFs) immobilization platform featuring a built-in electric field and a targeted Z-scheme electron transfer pathway. The CT-COF@Py-COF served as a mechanical scaffold for in situ encapsulation of reductases at the heterojunction interface, where electrostatic interactions, π–π stacking, and the ensuing formation of an interfacial electric field (IEF) collectively facilitated enzyme encapsulation. Moreover, IEF drove the conformational self-adaptation of encapsulated reductases and promoted directional charge transfer across the Z-scheme heterojunction, which synergistically enhanced catalytic activity and operational stability. The IEF-integrated system, paired with various dehydrogenases, enabled the efficient synthesis of pharmaceutical precursors under visible light. In a continuous-flow reactor, the encapsulated dehydrogenase retained approximately 88% of its initial-cycle glycine-production activity after eight cycles and exhibited a 7.18-fold increase in lactate yield when coupled with light-driven 1,4-NADH regeneration. This study provides a platform that utilizes IEF to dynamically confine enzymes’ self-adaptation in COF heterojunctions for photoenzymatic synthesis of high-value products.

title: Interfacial Electronic Regulation in N-Doped Carbon-Encapsulated NiCo Alloy Enables High-Current Nitrate-to-Ammonia Electrosynthesis
abstract: Abstract Electrochemical nitrate reduction (NO 3 − RR) offers a route to couple wastewater remediation with green ammonia (NH 3 ) synthesis, but remains kinetically and mechanistically challenging under high-current-density operation. Herein, an N-doped carbon-encapsulated NiCo alloy catalyst (NiCo@NC) is derived from a NiCo-ZB precursor supported on conductive carbon black. The cathodic NO 3 − RR over NiCo@NC achieves an NH 3 yield rate of 187 mol h −1 g cat −1 with 95% Faradaic efficiency (FE) at −0.6 V RHE in an H-type cell and sustains ~92% FE at 2.0 A cm −2 under a cell voltage of 3.3 V in a membrane–electrode assembly. Pairing this cathodic NO 3 − RR with anodic methanol oxidation to formate enables simultaneous NH 3 and formate production at 2.1 A cm −2 under a cell voltage of 2.8 V, while maintaining NH 3 and formate FEs above 90% and 96%, respectively. In situ Fourier transform infrared and operando X-ray absorption fine structure spectra reveal preferential *NO stabilization and reversible Co valence/coordination, while theoretical calculations disclose interfacial charge polarization between NiCo alloy core and N-doped carbon shell, fabricating dual sites, comprising electron-deficient graphitic carbon and electron-rich pyridinic-N domains, that accelerate water dissociation/proton supply and lower the barrier of the rate-determining *NO → *NOH step. These insights establish alloy@NC interface regulation as a general strategy for high-rate NO 3 − RR.

title: Flexible Hierarchical Porous Carbon Nanofibers/Aramid Nanofiber/ Ti 3 C 2 T x MXene Film for Electromagnetic Interference Shielding and Photothermal Conversion
abstract: ABSTRACT To address the challenge of simultaneously achieving high electromagnetic interference (EMI) shielding effectiveness and reduced electromagnetic wave reflection in MXene‐based materials, flexible composite films comprising hierarchically porous carbon nanofibers (HPCNFs), aramid nanofibers (ANF), and Ti 3 C 2 T x MXene were fabricated through vacuum‐assisted filtration and hot pressing. HPCNFs were introduced as a porous carbon component, while MXene served as a highly conductive shielding component. By regulating the assembly configuration, homogeneously mixed (H‐PAM) and laminated (L‐PAM) structures were constructed. The laminated architecture combined a porous HPCNFs/ANF layer with a conductive MXene layer. For electromagnetic wave incidence from the HPCNFs/ANF side, the optimized L‐PAM‐30 film exhibited an EMI shielding effectiveness of 31.8 dB, effectively blocking 99.93% of incident electromagnetic waves. Its reflection coefficient was 0.7154 for incidence from the HPCNFs/ANF side, compared with 0.955 for incidence from the ANF/MXene side. In addition, the composite films demonstrated mechanical flexibility, thermal stability, and photothermal conversion capability. This work provides an effective structural design strategy for reduced electromagnetic wave reflection in purely conductive MXene‐based shielding materials.

title: Pd Single‐Atom Engineered Janus BiOCl/MXene Heterostructure for Printed Self‐Decoupled Temperature‐Humidity Dual‐Mode Sensors
abstract: ABSTRACT The advancement of flexible sensing technologies is of paramount importance in biomedical engineering. However, achieving high‐fidelity multi‐modal temperature‐humidity sensing without inter‐channel cross‐talk and computational post‐processing remains a formidable challenge due to overlapping transduction mechanisms. In this study, an unprecedented electron‐ion synergistic functional material, featuring a unique inherent self‐decoupling capability, was developed based on the Janus hierarchical heterostructure. Through interfacial chemical engineering of Pd single‐atom anchoring and heterogeneous‐nucleation‐driven vertical growth of BiOCl on hollow MXene, the constructed material architecture successfully establishes fundamentally segregated electronic and ionic stimulus‐response pathways. Specifically, humidity fluctuations trigger ultra‐fast quasi‐2D proton conduction facilitated by localized potential wells and electronic redistribution generated around atomically dispersed Pd sites, while temperature gradients induce entropy‐driven carrier diffusion within the conductive MXene network. By suppressing signal cross‐talk through rigorous mechanistic orthogonality, the fabricated sensing array exhibits outstanding response characteristics (37.5/50 ms for humidity response/recovery and 25/62.5 ms for high/low‐temperature response), alongside superior oxidation resistance and robust functional durability (enduring 5000 cycles of testing). Ultimately, leveraging this multi‐modal sensing platform and machine learning algorithm, the integrated closed‐loop therapeutic system enables accurate evaluation of wound healing progression as well as on‐demand drug release, pioneering a new paradigm for next‐generation flexible electronics and adaptive healthcare modalities.

title: Maximizing the Photocatalytic Performance of Covalent Organic Frameworks by Decoupling Charge Separation and Recombination via Guest π-Conjugation
abstract: Abstract Covalent organic frameworks (COFs) have emerged as promising candidates for solar-driven photocatalysis; however, simultaneously achieving ultrafast electron–hole separation and suppressed charge recombination remains challenging. Here, we demonstrated a theory-guided design of high-performance host–guest COFs by tuning π-conjugation of embedded guest molecules. Combining many-body nonadiabatic molecular dynamics simulations based on linear response time-dependent density functional theory with transient spectroscopy and photocatalytic experiments, we elucidate the microscopic mechanisms governing excited-state dynamics in these systems. Our simulations suggest that increasing guest π-conjugation enables subpicosecond hole transfer from the COF host to the guest molecules by lowering the acceptor excitation energy and enhancing the density of acceptor states. Simultaneously, charge recombination is strongly suppressed through two synergistic effects. First, highly π-conjugated guests enhance low-frequency structural fluctuations and excited-state energetic disorder, thereby accelerating quantum decoherence. Second, increased guest π-conjugation promotes spatial separation of electrons and holes, while stronger instantaneous structural fluctuations under ambient conditions further localize charge carriers. These effects reduce electron–hole overlap and nonadiabatic coupling and markedly slow recombination relative to less conjugated systems. Femtosecond pump–probe spectroscopy supports the predicted guest-dependent differences in early excited-state dynamics. Guided by these mechanistic insights, we demonstrate experimentally that COFs incorporating highly conjugated guest molecules exhibit superior photocatalytic performance, achieving up to 97.38% conversion of 5-hydroxymethylfurfural with excellent product selectivity. The work establishes a molecular-level understanding of how guest properties govern excited-state dynamics in host–guest COFs and provides general design principles for developing high-performance photocatalysts.

title: Promoting photocatalytic methane oxidative coupling via gradient oxidation field engineering
abstract: Abstract The efficient and selective photocatalytic oxidative coupling of methane (OCM) into valuable chemicals remains an unresolved challenge in modern science. Herein, we report the design and synthesis of a robust photocatalyst by constructing photocatalytic gradient oxidation field on mesoporous TiO2, which demonstrates exceptional OCM performance and outperforms other benchmark photocatalysts. The optimized photocatalytic system exhibits a high CH4 conversion rate of 1.2 mmol h−1, a high C2 hydrocarbon space-time yield of 82.7 mmol g−1 h−1 and 90.1% C2 selectivity, accompanied by a remarkable apparent quantum efficiency of over 11.6%. Mechanism analyses reveal that the gradient oxidation field introduced by the Au nanoislands and Pd atomic satellites can optimize the oxidation activity and selectivity with hydroxide and superoxide radicals, respectively. The synergistic interaction between the Au and Pd sites facilitates favorable adsorption of O2/CH4 reactants and promotes fast desorption of the C2H6 product, thereby accelerating the overall OCM process. This work demonstrates the critical role of photocatalytic oxidation field, and opens a new avenue for developing efficient and selective catalysts for various photocatalytic applications.

title: Hierarchically Porous PDMS/ZIF-8@h-BN Bilayer Composite Membrane Enabling Synergistic Passive Daytime Radiative Cooling and Efficient Thermal Conduction for Electronic Thermal Management
abstract: Abstract The advancement of 5G and emerging 6G communications drives the integration and miniaturization of outdoor electronics, triggering an exponential surge in chip heat flux and severe challenges for low-energy passive thermal management. Passive daytime radiative cooling (PDRC) has emerged as a novel zero-energy cooling technology. Herein, a bilayer PDRC composite (B-PDRC) integrating radiative cooling and in-plane thermal conduction is designed and fabricated. The top radiative cooling layer is a hierarchically porous Polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS)/zeolitic imidazolate framework-8 (ZIF-8) foam prepared via a template-sacrificial method combined with vacuum impregnation, while the bottom thermally conductive layer is a PDMS/hexagonal boron nitride (h-BN) dense film fabricated by solution casting. The multiscale scattering induced by micron-sized pores and 600–800 nm ZIF-8 nanoparticles delivers a high solar reflectance of 94.45%, and the C–N bonds of ZIF-8 boost the average atmospheric window emissivity to 93.22%, compensating for the emissivity valley of neat PDMS. The h-BN fillers construct continuous thermal conduction paths, elevating the in-plane thermal conductivity to 0.92 W m–1 K–1 at 20 wt % of h-BN, a 179% enhancement compared to neat PDMS. Indoor tests demonstrate a maximum temperature drop of 11.9 °C for a charging smartphone covered with B-PDRC. Outdoor measurements under sunny conditions achieve a maximum subambient cooling of 8.8 °C, and a 14.8 °C temperature reduction for an operating smartphone. Furthermore, B-PDRC exhibits excellent hydrophobic self-cleaning performance (water contact angle of 135.4°), flexibility, mechanical robustness, long-term durability under UV and humid conditions, and universal adhesion to various substrates. This work provides a feasible design strategy for high-performance flexible PDRC composites for thermal management of outdoor electronic devices.

title: Single‐Step Orientational Self‐Assembly of Pd Metallacycles and Heterometallic Pd–Pt Helical Cages From Heteroditopic Ligands
abstract: ABSTRACT Controlling the self‐assembly of heterometallic supramolecular architectures without generating statistical mixtures remains a major challenge. Here, we show that adaptable coordination modes of tetrazole units in heterodipotic tetrazole–pyridine ligands direct both orientational self‐sorting and selective metal organization. Reaction with cis‐protected Pd(II) acceptors afforded Pd 6 ( L ) 4 metallacycles ( L = L1 – L3 ), in which tetrazolate coordination through an unusual (2,3) binding mode is exploited in the orientational self‐sorting. In contrast, ligand L4 employed its (1,3) coordination mode together with the pyridyl donors to generate a Pd 9 ( L4 ) 6 helical cage and the heterometallic Pd 9 Ag( L4 ) 6 , and Pd 3 Pt 6 ( L4 ) 6 cages in single‐step self‐assembly processes. Remarkably, despite the closely matched coordination preferences of Pd(II) and Pt(II), the synergistic effects of donor inequivalence and the flexible coordination behavior selectively partitions the two congeneric d 8 ions into distinct coordination sites within the Pd 3 Pt 6 ( L4 ) 6 cage. The uncommon (1,2,3) tetrazolate binding mode additionally enables formation of the Pd 9 Ag( L4 ) 6 cage. Encapsulation of enantiopure guests by the helical cages induces host chirality and corresponding chiroptical responses. These results demonstrate that coordination mode flexibility of the tetrazole moiety combined with the pyridyl unit can direct the formation of metallacycles and helical cages and enable selective partitioning of closely related metal ions in a single‐step assembly.

title: Partially reactive force field for the UiO-66 metal–organic framework
abstract: UiO-66 is the most widely studied metal-organic framework, on account of its structural tunability given by its capacity of sustaining high amounts of point defects in its structure. Its synthesis mechanism is largely unknown, with only a few works mostly focused on the formation of the Zr-oxide cluster. In this work, a partially reactive force field to model UiO-66, nb-UiO-FF, is introduced. This force field incorporates node-ligand reactivity via a Morse potential and the introduction of dummy atoms to reproduce the anisotropic charge distribution of the Zr atoms in the node. nb-UiO-FF reproduces structural features of both UiO-66 and its isoreticular analog UiO-67 as well as framework stability with or without defects, activated or filled with N,N-dimethylformamide or ethanol. Defect generation and node-ligand binding energies are comparable with density functional theory values. The force field is further employed within a molecular dynamics scheme to study the early stages of solvothermal node-ligand binding. Species with structures corresponding to motifs present in UiO-66 are observed, along with other metastable species. This force field enables studying the self-assembly of UiO-66, as well as the formation of its point defects.

title: Spin‐Polarized Metallic Metal−Organic Framework With High Conductivity and Half‐Metallic Behavior
abstract: ABSTRACT The establishment of new concepts for next‐generation conductive materials remains both highly desirable and scientifically challenging. Herein, we report a Cu‐based metal–organic framework (MOF), ([Cu(6Hmna)] n ( 1 , 6Hmna = 6‐mercaptonicotinic acid)), featuring metal–sulfur chains that exhibit intrinsic metallic behavior. Compound 1 exhibits a high electrical conductivity of up to 120 S cm−1, indicating a high electrical conductivity for a MOF in its crystalline form. The metallic transport characteristics are confirmed by temperature‐dependent conductivity measurements. In addition, this Cu‐MOF demonstrates highly efficient photoconductivity, with an outstanding photocurrent responsivity reaching 8100 A W −1 under infrared light illumination. Our theoretical DFT calculations predict that compound 1 exhibits an exotic spin‐polarized electronic structure, in which one spin channel is metallic while the other remains semiconducting. This unique electronic configuration is particularly attractive for applications in spintronics and quantum technologies, as well as in optoelectronic and photoelectrochemical devices.

title: Fe–Cu Bimetallic Metal–Organic Framework/Graphene Hybrid Electrodes for Advanced Supercapacitor Applications
abstract: Abstract In recent years, metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) have gained significant attention as efficient electrode materials for supercapacitors owing to their high specific surface area, tunable porous structure, and unique physicochemical properties. Herein, we demonstrate solvothermal synthesis of bimetallic Fe–Cu MOFs using iron and copper precursors and 2-aminoterephthalic acid as the organic linker. In order to overcome the inherent low electrical conductivity of MOFs, hybrids were prepared by incorporating reduced graphene oxide (rGO) at varying weight percentages. The main objective of the present study is to prepare supercapacitor electrodes by integrating the highly pseudocapacitive activity of the Fe–Cu MOFs with the excellent electrical properties of reduced graphene oxide. UV–vis, Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), X-ray diffraction (XRD), field-emission scanning electron microscopy (FESEM), and energy dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) characterization techniques confirmed the successful preparation of the Fe–Cu MOF/rGO hybrid. Electrochemical characterization showed that the FCG-10 (Fe–Cu MOF–10 wt % rGO) hybrid electrode exhibited a specific capacitance of 814.60 F g–1 at a scan rate of 5 mV s–1. Galvanostatic charge–discharge (GCD)-derived specific capacitance was found to be 706.85 F g–1 at 1 A g–1 in a three-electrode configuration. The FCG-10//rGO asymmetric supercapacitor, assembled using 1.30 mg of FCG-10 and 1.60 mg of rGO, showed a device-specific capacitance of 174.07 F g–1, an energy density of 28.19 Wh kg–1, and a power density of 539.80 W kg–1 at 1 A g–1. The FCG-10 electrode retained 91.8% of its initial capacitance after 10,000 GCD cycles in the three-electrode configuration. In a separate two-electrode FCG-10//rGO asymmetric device, the device retained 89.23% of its capacitance after 6000 cycles. The enhanced electrochemical performance can be ascribed to the synergistic effect of the highly porous Fe–Cu MOF and conductive reduced graphene oxide (rGO). The promising results demonstrate that the proposed approach provides an effective platform for the development of next-generation supercapacitor devices.

title: Stimuli-responsive mesoporous silica nanoparticle-based drug delivery systems
abstract: Mesoporous silica nanoparticles (MSNs) are versatile inorganic nanocarriers whose ordered mesopores, high surface area, tunable pore dimensions, and modifiable surfaces permit loading and controlled release of diverse therapeutic cargos. This review evaluates stimuli-responsive MSN design through an explicit evidence-grading lens: each proposed trigger is considered in relation to the primary study, biological model, demonstrated response, and principal limitation. Endogenous cues include pH, glutathione/redox conditions, reactive oxygen species, enzymes, glucose, ATP, and hypoxia; exogenous triggers include temperature, light, magnetic fields, and ultrasound. These cues can be coupled to molecular gates, cleavable linkers, responsive polymers, charge-reversal systems, or hybrid components. The review considers MSN architectures, synthesis and template removal, surface functionalization, drug loading and release, characterization, biological evaluation, and biomedical applications. Particular attention is paid to the distinction between chemical responsiveness and biological selectivity, and between in vitro , ex vivo , animal, and clinical evidence. Translational constraints include protein-corona formation, biological heterogeneity, biodistribution, intracellular trafficking, residual template or surfactant, sterilization, batch reproducibility, scale-up, and regulatory complexity. Emerging biodegradable and biomimetic MSNs, nucleic-acid delivery, theranostics, precision nanomedicine, and data-assisted formulation development are treated as developing rather than uniformly established technologies. The review’s contribution is a comparative framework for asking whether each added responsive function produces a measurable benefit over a simpler carrier, rather than assuming that greater structural complexity improves therapeutic performance. The evidence-based framework used here distinguishes the level of testing from the strength of the claim: in vitro release or cell data establish proof of concept, ex vivo data address selected tissue-level behavior, animal studies provide preclinical evidence, and clinical evidence requires human evaluation of the specific responsive MSN system. Clinical experience with other silica-containing materials is not equivalent to clinical validation of stimuli-responsive MSN drug carriers. Key translational questions include predictable degradation and clearance, control of manufacturing-related impurities, reproducible critical quality attributes, clinically relevant trigger intensity, and demonstrated safety and efficacy in appropriate models.

title: Unlocking Intrinsic Chirality in Luminescent Copper Clusters via Intramolecular Spatial Confinement
abstract: Abstract Most luminescent clusters that exhibit pronounced chiral signals typically rely on predesigned chiral ligands; however, stimulating the intrinsic chirality of clusters in the absence of exogenous asymmetric ligands remains a significant challenge. In this study, based on a series of structure-correlated Cu2 clusters, we demonstrate that intramolecular spatial confinement effectively induces distortions in flexible ligands, thereby imparting asymmetry to the cluster framework. This molecular asymmetry further determines the orientation of cluster entities during supramolecular assembly, thus enabling the modulation of chirality across this cluster series between inactive (“off”) and active (“on”) states. In addition, these structure-correlated Cu2 clusters display bright and tunable luminescence, allowing for the fabrication of uniform thin films that function as practical scintillation materials for high-resolution X-ray imaging. Collectively, this work provides a novel perspective for regulating the chiroptical properties of metal clusters through the activation of intramolecular spatial confinement and offers valuable insights into the fabrication of cluster-based nanomaterials with tailored photophysical performances.

title: CHARMM-Compatible Molecular Mechanics Force Fields for Multiscale Modeling of HIV-1 Replication Inhibitors
abstract: Abstract Molecular dynamics simulations provide insight into inhibitor-protein interactions and support rational drug design; however, their accuracy depends on reliable molecular mechanics force field parameters and coarse-grained representations that retain relevant molecular features. Although force field parameter sets for biomacromolecules are well established, the chemical diversity of small-molecule inhibitors often requires the development of system-specific parameters. Here, we present a parametrization framework integrating quantum mechanical optimization, experimental benchmarking, and small-molecule coarse-graining, demonstrated using HIV-1 inhibitors targeting multiple stages of the viral replication cycle. We provide a curated data set of CHARMM-compatible force field parameters for 12 HIV-1 inhibitors and the HIV assembly cofactor inositol hexakisphosphate (IP6), together with geometry-optimized atomic structures and ligand restraint files. The resulting parameters are validated against experimental structural and thermodynamic benchmarks, including lenacapavir binding free energy estimates, through inhibitor-bound complex simulations. We demonstrate applications of the parameter data set by quantifying inhibitor-protein interactions, including the free-energy profile of an integrase strand transfer inhibitor interacting with the viral capsid lattice, and the binding energetics of an allosteric integrase inhibitor. Furthermore, we extend the all-atom inhibitor parameter data set through a novel coarse-graining strategy for small molecules that preserves key electrostatic features. The HIV-1 inhibitor force field parameter data set is a publicly available resource that establishes a unified framework for multiscale modeling of HIV-1 inhibitors and facilitates computational and structural biology studies of drug resistance and inhibitor design. More generally, the framework presented here is broadly applicable to small-molecule parametrization and multiscale simulations in other therapeutic and biomolecular contexts.

title: Electrostatic Cation Intercalation Into Polymeric Self‐Assembled Monolayers Enables Ambient‐Air Fabrication of 32.73% Efficient Monolithic Perovskite/Silicon Tandem Solar Cells
abstract: ABSTRACT Polymeric self‐assembled monolayers (SAMs) enable stable, efficient, and scalable perovskite/silicon tandem solar cells (TSCs) based on silicon heterojunction (HJT) bottom cells. However, severe steric hindrance within the polymer matrix disrupts the directional anchoring of phosphonate groups, thereby limiting macroscopic work‐function regulation and sustaining a persistent hole‐extraction barrier. Herein, we report a targeted molecular reconstruction of the buried interface via the electrostatic intercalation of phenethylammonium iodide (PEAI). Templated by the polymer backbone, the intercalated PEA + cations adopt a highly directional vertical arrangement. This oriented molecular scaffold provides a strong intrinsic dipole while driving the electronegative iodide (I − ) counterions to enrich at the uppermost interface. This synergistic spatial decoupling maximizes the net upward dipole, triggering a favorable energy level realignment that effectively overcomes the hole extraction barrier. Concurrently, the halide‐enriched SAM dictates crystallization kinetics during ambient‐air slot‐die coating, inducing rapid “burst nucleation” to minimize solvate intermediates and suppress basal voids. Consequently, our 1 cm 2 TSC achieves an independently certified power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 32.73%. Benefiting from monolithic crystallographic integrity, the unencapsulated device maintains an enhanced T 80 lifetime of 2182 h under continuous maximum power point tracking.

title: Monomer Flexibility Enables the Regulation of Interlayer Stacking in Two-Dimensional Covalent Organic Frameworks
abstract: Abstract Precise control over interlayer stacking in two-dimensional covalent organic frameworks (2D COFs) remains far less developed than the design of in-plane topology. Here, rather than regulating stacking through external changes in the crystallization medium, we investigate the conformational compatibility of paired monomers as an internal molecular variable for directing the out-of-plane organization of 2D COFs. A topologically related series of eight imine-linked COFs was constructed using different combinations of flexible and rigid monomers. Within the present COF series, flexible-flexible monomer combinations were associated with AA′ stacking, whereas flexible-rigid combinations were associated with ABC stacking. These distinct stacking outcomes are associated with different conformational responses during framework formation. The resulting stacking-defined pore environments further give rise to different xylene adsorption and separation behaviors, with the AA′-stacked COFs showing enhanced discrimination among xylene isomers. This work identifies monomer flexibility matching as an important molecular design consideration for regulating interlayer stacking, extending 2D COF design from in-plane topology to out-of-plane structural control.

title: Fabrication of Ni–BTC/GO nanocomposite membrane for removing common pesticides and heavy metals
abstract: Abstract The development of advanced membrane materials is crucial for removing hazardous pollutants from contaminated water. In this study, a nickel-based metal–organic framework (Ni–BTC) was combined with graphene oxide (GO) to produce a Ni–BTC/GO nanocomposite with superior removal performance for heavy metals and pesticides. GO was synthesized using a rapid and environmentally friendly electrochemical exfoliation of graphite, followed by in situ growth of Ni–BTC on the GO scaffold through a solvothermal method. The oxygen-containing functional groups on GO interacted strongly with the nickel centers, leading to a homogeneous dispersion of Ni–BTC particles and the formation of a hierarchically porous hybrid structure. The successful formation of the composite was confirmed by XRD, FTIR, SEM, BET, Zeta potential, and TGA analyses. The Ni–BTC/GO composite membrane was evaluated using a dead‑end filtration cell. The membrane achieved removal efficiencies (rejection rates) of 92.4% for Pb 2+ , 89.7% for Cd 2+ , 87.5% for α‑cypermethrin, and 84.3% for acetamiprid, surpassing the performance of pure Ni–BTC and GO membranes. The material also retained its rejection performance after three cycles, indicating good reusability and structural stability. This study demonstrates the application of Ni–BTC/GO membranes for simultaneous rejection of heavy metals and pesticides, combining green GO synthesis with pressure‑driven filtration.

title: Slit-Confined Self-Assembly of Cellulose Nanocrystals for Long-Range Ordered Cholesteric Architecture
abstract: Abstract Long-range ordered cellulose nanocrystal (CNC) architectures are vital for photonic applications, but conventional self-assembly predominantly yields defective, multidomain nanostructures. Herein, this study proposes a slit-confined self-assembly (SCSA) strategy to construct a scalable CNC cholesteric liquid crystal structure with a single orientational domain. Distinct from conventional methods relying on extreme external fields or drying protocols, SCSA utilizes a simple glass slit to steer CNC assembly through synergistic physical effects: gravity drives tactoids sedimentation and interfacial hydrogen bonding enforces preferential alignment. Concurrently, the geometric constraint effectively suppresses the nucleation and propagation of topological defects, enabling the formation of centimeter-scale monodomain cholesteric architectures. As a result, brilliant structural color in aqueous CNC suspensions is achieved without external fields or active stimuli, enabled solely by the synergistic effects of geometric confinement, gravity-driven sedimentation, and interfacial hydrogen-bond anchoring. The resulting highly ordered architecture achieves an exceptional orientation factor of 0.98 and a structural color dissymmetry factor (g) as high as 1.3, accompanied by reversible structural reassembly behavior. Furthermore, upon coassembling with luminescent guests, the system exhibits a giant circularly polarized luminescence (CPL) dissymmetry factor (glum) reaching −1.1. Collectively, this work establishes a robust, straightforward, and scalable route for highly controllable liquid crystal self-assembly, offering promising avenues toward high-performance photonic applications.

title: A Single‐COF Photocatalytic System for One‐Pot Oxygen Reduction Coupled Ammoximation of Cyclic Ketones
abstract: ABSTRACT Photocatalytic oxygen reduction over covalent organic frameworks (COFs) has been extensively studied for H 2 O 2 production, but the in situ utilization of oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) intermediates in chemical synthesis remains underexplored. Herein, two porphyrin‐based polyimide COFs, IMCOF‐1 and IMCOF‐2, are reported as photocatalysts for the one‐pot ORR‐coupled ammoximation of cyclic ketones using O 2 and NH 4 OAc. Under light irradiation, IMCOF‐1 achieves a cyclohexanone oxime formation rate of 18.55 mmol g −1 h −1 and is effective for several other cyclic ketones. Mechanistic investigations reveal that photoinduced electron transfer from the porphyrin units to the electron‐deficient imide moieties promotes charge separation and activates O 2 at the carbonyl sites. The resulting surface‐bound *OOH intermediates are proposed to participate in ammonia oxidation and subsequent NH 2 OH formation, which then condenses with cyclic ketones to yield the corresponding oximes. In contrast to stepwise systems that first accumulate H 2 O 2 before ammoximation, the present one‐pot strategy enables the in situ utilization of oxygen‐derived reactive intermediates without requiring substantial bulk H 2 O 2 pre‐accumulation, eliminating the need for H 2 O 2 isolation, storage, and transport, thereby improving safety and atom economy while maintaining high selectivity. This work demonstrates the potential of directly harnessing ORR‐derived intermediates for the light‐driven synthesis of value‐added nitrogen‐containing chemicals.

title: A Synthetic Journey Toward Functional N ‐Amidophenyl‐Substituted Hexaaza[1 6 ]paracyclophanes
abstract: Conjugated macrocycles hold great promises for applications as photo‐ and electroactive materials. In particular, aza‐[1 n ]paracyclophane was recently described to reach high electrical conductivity in single‐crystal devices due to their tubular assemblies. However, the self‐assembly of these macrocycles in solution and in thin films remains a challenge. Our group reported recently that properly‐designed hexaaza[1 6 ]paracyclophane molecules can self‐assemble in nanotubular structures which can delocalize electrons both through bond within the macrocycle and through space along the supramolecular structure. Nevertheless, accessing these macrocyclic molecules with lateral amide moieties is not straightforward. In this paper, we report the various synthetic strategies we designed to access N ‐amidophenyl‐substituted hexaaza[1 6 ]paracyclophane using Cu‐catalyzed Ullmann coupling and Pd‐catalyzed Buchwald–Hartwig reactions as key steps. The synthetic sequences were designed to reach exclusively 6‐membered macrocycles, to limit purification processes to classical column chromatographies, and to provide ~100 mg scale quantities. The optimized synthetic route allowed to study the light‐responsive properties of a 6‐membered triarylamine‐based macrocycle, following procedures originally developed for simpler triarylamine molecules.

title: Concentration‐Dependent Self‐Assembly and Nanoparticle Maturation of Reflectins
abstract: ABSTRACT Cephalopods dynamically modulate coloration for camouflage and communication through iridophores whose Bragg reflector‐like ultrastructures contain high‐refractive‐index proteins known as reflectins. However, the mechanisms linking concentration, conformation, and nanoparticle stabilization in full‐length reflectins remain poorly understood. Here, coarse‐grained molecular dynamics simulations of Doryteuthis pealeii reflectin A2 (RfA2) across five concentrations are combined with dynamic light scattering (DLS) and circular dichroism (CD) measurements. The simulations reveal rapid initial protein aggregation followed by slower structural maturation, during which interprotein interaction energy and contact networks continue to evolve. A simulation‐derived concentration‐dependent crossover separates multi‐cluster vs single‐cluster regimes and DLS shows larger assemblies at higher experimental concentrations. The simulations further delineate region‐specific secondary‐structure reorganization and CD demonstrates concentration‐sensitive structural changes with a distinct secondary‐structure redistribution. Moreover, the simulations predict concentration dependence in the contribution of intermolecular contact network reorganization; the L1, L3, and L5 linker regions supplied many of these contacts, with L3 providing the dominant contribution. Overall, these findings establish a molecular‐level framework where concentration governs RfA2 self‐assembly and continued conformational and intermolecular reorganization during maturation, providing insight into sequence‐ and assembly‐level principles regarding iridophore optical function and reflectin‐based materials design.

title: Self-Assembly of Two-Dimensional Open Structures with Adjustable Square Voids
abstract: Abstract Self-assembly of anisotropic particles offers a powerful route to design materials with tailored microstructures. Here we investigate two-dimensional systems of patchy hard rectangles using Monte Carlo simulations and free volume theory, mapping their phase diagram across packing fractions and interaction strengths. Low attraction recovers excluded-volume phase behavior (isotropic–tetratic–smectic), while intermediate attraction strengths feature a broad isotropic–smectic coexistence region. For high interaction strengths our theory predicts, and simulations confirm, a highly ordered “weaver” phase characterized by a four-rectangle unit cell that forms a regular grid of square voids. Although the pure weaver phase forms only in a narrow window of packing fractions, it coexists with either the isotropic gas or smectic solid over a wide range of packing fractions. Patchy rectangles demonstrate how shape together with tunable interactions can be utilized to self-assemble porous materials with precisely adjustable void sizes and geometries and could be realized using DNA origami structures.

title: Mechanochemical Synthesis and Co‐Former–Controlled Assembly of Azobenzene Polycarboxylate Organic Salts: From Framework Node to Passive Guest in HOF‐Like Architectures
abstract: ABSTRACT Hydrogen‐bonded organic salts are versatile supramolecular materials whose architecture can be tuned through co‐former selection. Here, we report two multicomponent crystals of the azobenzene polycarboxylic acid 4,4′‐(diazene‐1,2‐diyl)bis(3,5‐dicarboxybenzoic acid) ( DADIA ): one with imidazole ( DADIA:IMD2 ) and one with N ‐methylimidazole ( DADIA:MeIMD ). Both were prepared by mechanochemical grinding followed by recrystallization from methanol. In each case, proton transfer from the carboxylic acid groups to the imidazole nitrogen gives charge‐assisted N + –H···O − hydrogen bonds, so the materials are best described as organic salts. Single‐crystal x‐ray diffraction shows that DADIA:IMD2 crystallizes in a monoclinic ( C2/c ) and DADIA:MeIMD in a triclinic ( P‐1 ), both forming two‐dimensional HOF‐like architectures. In DADIA:IMD2 , protonated imidazole acts as an active network node, generating channels occupied by disordered solvent. In DADIA:MeIMD , the 2D sheet is stabilized by O–H···O bonding between DADIA host molecules, with protonated N ‐methylimidazole housed in the pores as a passive guest. The compounds were further characterized by 1 H NMR, FT‐IR, PXRD, and TGA. These results show how a single N ‐methyl substituent switches the co‐former between the network node and the guest, with implications for gas storage, separation, and drug delivery.

title: Multiphase Inorganic-Rich Interphases with Integrated Li-Ion Capture-Transport Ability for High-Rate Lithium Metal Batteries
abstract: Abstract Lithium metal batteries promise high-energy-density storage but are limited by unstable solid–electrolyte interphases, which couple poor passivation, sluggish Li+ transport, dendritic deposition, and safety risks. Herein, we report a multiphase inorganic-rich solid–electrolyte interphase (m-SEI) containing P- and Al-derived species including Li3P, LiAl5O8, Li3PO4, and Li2Al, which is formed from the in situ reaction between a flame-retardant aluminum diethyl hypophosphite (ADP) interlayer and lithium metal. This multicomponent inorganic SEI enables an integrated capture-transport mechanism by combining high Li+ affinity, facilitated desolvation, and low-barrier Li+ migration pathways in individual inorganic phases and their heterophase interfaces, thereby facilitating rapid Li+ interfacial migration. Its chemical inertness and high Young’s modulus of 17.14 GPa further suppress electrolyte decomposition and Li dendrite growth. As a result, the Li-metal batteries with m-SEI deliver an extended lifespan of 1000 h at a high current density of 4 mA cm–2. Li||NCM811 full cells with a high cathode loading (20 mg cm–2) and ultrathin Li foil (50 μm) retain 80% capacity after 250 cycles, while Li||NCM811 pouch cells retain 90% capacity after 500 cycles. This work establishes the capture-transport mechanism as an effective design principle for regulating Li+ interfacial dynamics and offers a practical interphase-engineering strategy for constructing ion-conductive and chemically protective interphases in durable lithium metal batteries.

title: Intrinsically Stretchable Fully π‐Conjugated Polymer Films Enabled by Supramolecular Plasticized Micro‐Crosslinking‐Network for Flexible Polymer Light‐Emitting Diodes
abstract: ABSTRACT Stretchable fully π‐conjugated polymers (FπCPs) films with a fantastic optoelectronic property and outstanding deformation tolerance capacity, is a promising candidate for the fabrication of flexible optoelectronics devices. However, previous reported stretchable FπCPs films undergo irreversible chain slippage and alignment upon strain release, leading to plastic deformation, and consequently severe performance degradation during cyclic‐deformation operation. Herein, we proposed a supramolecular soft‐micro‐crosslinked strategy to achieve the stretchable p ‐ n FπCPs (P X ‐OXI 1‐X ‐HDI) films with a recoverable‐deformation ability for the flexible electronics. Three‐dimensional (3D) supramolecular micro‐crosslinked network formed by oxime‐urethane and hydrogen bonds allow for the excellent elastic deformation to dissipate transient stress while fundamentally suppressing permanent chain slippage. Micro‐crosslinked p ‐ n FπCPs free‐standing films achieved an elongation at break of > 40%. Flexible PLED based on P X ‐OXI 1‐X ‐HDI showed a stable green emission with brightness of ∼3300 cd cm −2 . Meanwhile, the performance of transferred PLED based on stretchable micro‐crosslinked films are independent on the tensile ratio (>20%) with a maximum brightness of ∼2000 cd m −2 , revealed the excellent cycle‐deformation‐stability than device based on crosslinked films. Therefore, these supramolecular micro‐crosslinked networks can enhance instantaneous toughness and confer a critical resistance to long‐term stress relaxation and plastic deformation, further ensure the device excellent deformation stability.

title: Beyond acceptor emissivity: interfacial excited-state energetics and dynamic disorder regulate nonradiative voltage losses for organic solar cells
abstract: Abstract Suppressing non-radiative energy loss (ΔEnr) is critical for achieving high open-circuit voltage (VOC) in organic solar cells (OSCs), yet it remains unclear whether intrinsic emissive properties of acceptors can reliably predict voltage losses. Here, we report a counterintuitive phenomenon in which a low-emissive acceptor (D6) delivers a significantly reduced ΔEnr compared with the benchmark L8-BO when blended with D18. Despite lower intrinsic emissivity of D6, the D18: D6 system exhibits a markedly higher electroluminescence efficiency and a reduced ΔEnr of 0.153 eV, leading to an enhanced VOC of 0.980 V. Incorporation of D6 into the D18: L8-BO host yields a ternary device with a power conversion efficiency of 21.01%. Sensitive EQE analysis reveals that favorable CT-state energetics partially contribute to the reduced non-radiative loss of D18: D6, while temperature-dependent photoluminescence analysis further identifies suppressed interfacial dynamic disorder as a critical additional factor. While dynamic disorder is significantly increased in the D18: L8-BO blend, it is effectively suppressed in the D18: D6 system, resulting in preserved emissive interfacial states. Complementary structural and kinetic studies demonstrate that D6 modulates aggregation pathways and stabilizes nanoscale morphology, enabling efficient charge transport and reduced recombination. Furthermore, the beneficial role of D6 can be extended to multiple high-performance acceptor systems, demonstrating its general applicability as an interfacial regulator for improving photovoltaic performance. These results highlight that non-radiative voltage loss in OSCs is governed by the interplay between interfacial excited-state energetics and dynamic disorder rather than by the intrinsic emissivity of the acceptor alone, providing new insights into the design of low-energy-loss photovoltaic materials.

title: X-Shaped Multichannel Conjugation Enabled by Excited-State Aromaticity
abstract: Abstract Molecular topology governs the photophysical properties of polycyclic π-conjugated systems by defining their effective conjugation pathways. Conventionally, linear π-extension is considered more effective than angular extension in increasing the effective conjugation length and narrowing the optical bandgap. Here we uncover an inverse topology–property relationship in π-extended dihydrophenazines (DHPs): linear extension unexpectedly blueshifts fluorescence, whereas angular extension produces pronounced redshifts. Transient spectroscopy, theoretical calculations and aromaticity analyses reveal that Baird aromaticity–driven planarization of the DHP core redistributes π-delocalization in the S1 state, causing linear fusion to disrupt global π-delocalization and shorten the effective conjugation length, while angular fusion promotes cooperative delocalization across the fused framework and extends it. Successive angular fusion progressively activates four structurally distinct π-extension branches through the shared Baird-aromatic DHP core, generating an X-shaped multichannel conjugation network. These findings reveal how excited-state aromaticity reprograms conjugation topology, offering new insights for controlling π-delocalization and emission.

title: Rate Capability of Lithium‐Rich Manganese‐Based Oxide Cathodes: Charge–Discharge Kinetics, Multiscale Bottlenecks, and Dynamic Rate‐Determining Steps
abstract: ABSTRACT Lithium‐rich manganese‐based oxide (LRMO) cathode materials deliver a reversible specific capacity exceeding 250 mAh g −1 through synergistic anionic and cationic redox, promising for next‐generation high‐energy‐density batteries, yet their poor rate capability remains a critical barrier to practical deployment, particularly for fast‐charging applications. This review deconstructs rate‐limiting mechanisms at three levels, namely direct charge‐transport impediments, kinetic sluggishness of anionic redox, and degradation cascade of phase transformations, voltage decay, and microcracking that exacerbates kinetics. A central insight is that the rate‐determining step (RDS) shifts from electron‐transfer to ion‐diffusion dominance, governed by the exchange current density ( j 0 ) and the limiting current density ( j d ). Modification strategies are classified into two threads, kinetic enhancement by shortening diffusion paths and lowering migration barriers, and structural stabilization by reinforcing bonds and suppressing oxygen release. Importantly, the often‐overlooked charging kinetics are critically assessed, as the asymmetric nature of anionic redox imposes a more severe bottleneck for fast charging than for high‐rate discharging. Methodological limitations in cross‐study C‐rate comparisons, arising from variations in electrode loading and testing protocols, are also examined to enable more rigorous evaluation of reported performance. This review ultimately provides a theoretical foundation for rational design of high‐rate LRMO cathodes toward practical energy storage applications.

title: Microneedles Fabrication by Substrate‐Independent Electrostretching and In‐Situ Focused Electrospray Deposition for Transdermal Drug Delivery
abstract: ABSTRACT Universal transdermal drug delivery remains constrained by the material dependencies and fabrication complexities of current microneedle (MN) technologies. Here, we present the innovative substrate‐independent pulsating in situ dried electrostretching (SI‐PIDES) and the in situ focused electrospray deposition (IFED) platform capable of fabricating and precisely coating MNs on flexible, non‐conductive dielectric patches. By leveraging polarized pulsed voltage, these methods enable the mold‐free fabrication of polymeric MNs and the precise coating of drug‐loaded substances onto dielectric MN patches. This novel discovery provides an integrated and simplified workflow for MN patch fabrication. Experimental results demonstrate that SI‐PIDES and IFED produce mechanically robust core–sheath microneedles and gain considerable improvements in deposition accuracy. Multiphysics particle simulations revealed the effects of charge accumulation on the non‐conductive MN and confirmed the crucial role of the polarized voltage in maintaining deposition efficiency. We further demonstrate the practical utility of this platform by synthesizing and coating zinc/magnesium‐doped mesoporous silica nanoparticles as a drug model, which showed excellent biocompatibility and potent antibacterial suppression in in vitro assays. These findings emphasize the potential of our technology as a simple and physics‐driven approach for the development of scalable, next‐generation high‐precision transdermal drug delivery systems.

title: Radical C─N Coupling at Electrified Carbon Nanotube Interfaces
abstract: ABSTRACT Nitrogen‐containing motifs are central to pharmaceuticals, materials, and bioactive molecules, yet controlling radical C─N bond formation under mild and catalyst‐free conditions remains challenging. Here, we report an electrified carbon nanotube (CNT) interface that promotes radical C─N coupling of aniline derivatives and N ‐containing heterocyclic compounds under ambient conditions. Mechanistic experiments show that the enhanced reactivity arises from the coupling of the applied electric field with interfacial charge transfer through the CNT network. Radical trapping, redox probing, and density functional theory calculations support a field‐assisted electron‐transfer pathway involving nitrogen‐centered radical intermediates. Our results indicate that the applied field lowers the barrier to radical generation, underscoring its critical role in enabling the reaction. This work demonstrates that conductive nanointerfaces can enable localized radical bond‐forming chemistry under an externally applied electric field.

title: Mononuclear and Dinuclear Nickel Sites on Periodic Mesoporous Silica for CO2 Cycloaddition to Epoxides
abstract: Abstract The development of efficient heterogeneous catalysts for converting carbon dioxide into value-added products under mild conditions remains an important challenge. Herein, we report the synthesis of mono- and dinuclear Ni-functionalized materials through stepwise grafting onto periodic mesoporous silica (SBA-15). The materials were systematically constructed via aminosilane functionalization, ligand immobilization, and subsequent coordination of Ni centers, and were comprehensively characterized by several techniques, including PXRD, SEM/TEM, EA, ICP-OES, DRIFT-IR, N2 physisorption, XPS, and solid-state MAS NMR, confirming the successful formation of well-defined surface-bound Ni species. The resulting catalysts were evaluated for the cycloaddition of CO2 to epoxides. The immobilized dinuclear nickel naphthyridine diimine material (Ni2-NDI@SBA-15250) exhibited superior catalytic performance compared with its mononuclear nickel phenanthroline-derived analogue (Ni-PhenDI@SBA-15250) and the corresponding homogeneous systems, achieving high to full conversions and &gt;99% selectivity under relatively mild conditions (80 °C, 10 bar CO2) with only 0.1 mol % Ni. The enhanced activity is consistent with cooperative interactions between adjacent Ni centers, combined with the confinement effects of the ordered mesoporous structure. Furthermore, the catalyst demonstrated good stability and recyclability, with negligible metal leaching as confirmed by hot filtration and ICP analysis. This work highlights the potential of heterogenizing multinuclear Ni complexes within mesoporous frameworks for efficient CO2 utilization and provides insight into the design of robust heterogeneous catalysts for sustainable transformations.

title: Topologically Rigidified Chiral Ionic Organic Crystals for High-Resolution Gas Chromatographic Separation
abstract: Abstract Chiral ionic organic crystals (CIOCs) have emerged as promising candidates for enantioseparation in gas chromatography (GC); however, conventional porous stationary phase materials often suffer from an intrinsic trade-off between efficient mass transfer within pores and sufficient stereochemical recognition. Herein, we present a conjugated structure-directed topological rigidification strategy for the rational engineering of CIOCs. Three CIOCs, BPDS-DBIM, TPDS-DBIM and TPDS-DBPIM, were constructed by regulating the conjugation length of ionic building blocks, revealing a progressive evolution from flexible ionic porous single crystals to highly ordered rigid channel architectures. The extension of conjugated backbones effectively reorganized the packing modes of cations and anions, leading to enhanced framework stability and tunable confined chiral microenvironments. Through further optimization of the molecular architecture, TPDS-DBPIM exhibited a more rigid framework with well-defined microporous features, indicating enhanced structural rigidity and stability relative to the less rigid ionic assembly. When used as the stationary phase in capillary GC, TPDS-DBPIM demonstrates superior enantiomeric separation performance, enabling efficient separation of 17 structurally distinct chiral drugs and a variety of chiral intermediates. Comprehensive thermodynamic and kinetic investigations further revealed that the rigidly confined microporous architecture serves as the key driving force governing the enhanced chiral recognition and mass-transfer behavior. This work addresses the long-standing mass transport and recognition trade-off in porous chromatographic materials and provides a molecular engineering paradigm for the development of next-generation high-resolution enantioseparation media.

title: Mechanisms and Structural Regulation of Metal–Organic Framework Materials for Photocatalytic CO 2 Reduction
abstract: Photocatalytic CO 2 reduction can convert CO 2 into high-value chemicals and fuels such as CO, HCOOH, CH 3 OH, and CH 4 by utilizing solar energy, representing an important pathway for carbon resource utilization. Metal-organic frameworks (MOFs), with their tunable metal nodes, organic linkers, and regular pore structures, exhibit unique advantages in CO 2 enrichment, light absorption, charge transport, and stabilization of key intermediates. This review focuses on the mechanisms and structural regulation of MOFs for photocatalytic CO 2 reduction. It first introduces the fundamental processes of photogenerated carrier generation and migration, CO 2 adsorption and activation, proton-coupled electron transfer, and product formation. It then summarizes representative MOF systems based on Zr, Fe, and Ti, as well as the performance characteristics of composites with metal nanoparticles, molecular catalysts, and semiconductors. On this basis, it further analyzes the influence mechanisms of metal-node regulation, linker functionalization, defect engineering, pore-microenvironment modulation, and heterointerface construction on light absorption, charge separation, intermediate adsorption, and product selectivity. Existing studies indicate that the photocatalytic performance of MOFs depends on the synergistic matching of their electronic structure, active sites, and local reaction microenvironment. Future efforts should address challenges including photogenerated charge recombination, structural stability, and selectivity in multi-electron reactions, while combining in situ characterization and theoretical calculations to deepen the understanding of real active sites and reaction pathways, thereby providing a theoretical basis for the rational design of efficient and stable MOF photocatalysts and CO 2 resource utilization.

title: Crystalline NiO:N Templating of Uniformly Anchored Self-Assembled Monolayers for Inverted Perovskite Solar Cells
abstract: Abstract The buried hole-selective contact in inverted perovskite solar cells (PSCs) is expected to transport holes through its bulk while also templating a defect-free self-assembled monolayer (SAM). A crystalline, vacuum-deposited nitrogen-doped NiO (NiO:N) film deterministically templates a uniformly anchored SAM, while the reactive-atmosphere N2/O2 ratio used during pulsed laser deposition (PLD) simultaneously programs bulk hole density and interfacial anchoring chemistry. Nitrogen incorporation is proposed to act as a shallow acceptor that generates Ni3+ states and raises p-type conductivity, whereas the dense, pinhole-free template enforces uniform SAM coverage, fully suppressing the underlying substrate signal and minimizing surface hydroxyl groups relative to discontinuous nanoparticle films. Consequently, NiO:N/SAM-based PSCs achieve a 6.2% relative increase in power conversion efficiency (PCE) over pristine NiO nanoparticles, reaching one of the highest reported performances for vacuum-deposited NiO-based PSCs, with improved thermal and operational stability. These results establish reactive-atmosphere NiO:N as a general, scalable platform for hole-selective contacts in inverted perovskite photovoltaics.

title: Plasmon-Defined Chemical Templates for the Nanoscale Assembly of Colloidal Nanoparticles
abstract: Abstract Controlling matter with nanoscale spatial selectivity is a key hurdle for plasmonic applications such as nanophotonics, sensing, and catalysis. Plasmon-assisted nanolithography has recently emerged as a powerful strategy to address this challenge by exploiting the highly confined electromagnetic fields and hot carriers generated during plasmon excitation to confine organic or inorganic layers at the nanoscale. Among the surface chemistries compatible with this approach, aryl diazonium salts are particularly attractive because their reduction produces highly reactive aryl radicals that form robust covalent bonds with metallic surfaces under mild conditions. Under light excitation, the plasmon-induced reduction of aryl diazonium salts enables the rapid and site-selective grafting of functional organic layers confined to plasmonic hot spots. The resulting functional films provide versatile chemical handles for further modification. However, to date, the use of plasmon-mediated diazonium grafting as a spatially controlled primer layer to direct the site-selective immobilization of colloidal nanoparticles remains unexplored. We address this gap by using lithographic gold nanodisc arrays as optically programmable templates. Under plasmon excitation, these nanostructures enable the formation of positively charged nanoscale anchoring domains at plasmonic hot spots, derived from diazonium salts bearing amine groups. These localized charged domains can then guide the spatial organization of negatively charged colloidal gold nanoparticles. The geometrical parameters of the plasmonic arrays, including nanodisc diameter and interparticle spacing, were carefully tuned to access different plasmon excitation regimes around the 633 nm laser wavelength, enabling blue-shifted, near-resonant, and red-shifted conditions, and expanding the variety of achievable hybrid patterns. Complementary characterization using SEM, UV−vis spectroscopy, and FDTD simulations demonstrates that this approach provides a straightforward and versatile strategy to direct the assembly of colloidal nanoparticles on lithographic nanostructures via optical excitation.

title: Emulsion-Mediated Self-Assembly of Au Nanoparticles at Liquid–Liquid Interface: A Kinetics Perspective
abstract: Emulsion-mediated self-assembly of nanoparticles at liquid–liquid interfaces has been established, yet its particle adsorption kinetics remain largely unexplored. In this study, we investigate particle adsorption during this process by sonicating Au colloids with an oil phase. Unlike a planar water–oil interface, which poses a finite sorption energy barrier, the curved interfaces of droplets substantially lower this barrier, thereby switching the adsorption regime from kinetic control to diffusion control. In this scenario, sonication generates emulsions with a huge total water–oil interfacial area, may accelerate mass transport (acting as an agitator), and may also activate particles to overcome the residual (if any) barrier, all of which synergistically enhance particle adsorption. Furthermore, optical observations could reveal that the droplet surfaces are sparsely decorated with particle aggregates, leaving ample free area for further unimpeded adsorption, and coalescence of particle-laden droplets continuously releases particles to the planar water–oil interface, where they form a compact film. Our results might highlight effective means to enhance particle adsorption for subsequent interfacial assembly of nanoparticles.

title: Applications of Directed Self-Assembly Lithography in Advanced Semiconductor Devices
abstract: As semiconductor devices continue to scale down, conventional lithography technologies face increasingly severe challenges in resolution, stochastic defect control, and manufacturing cost. Block copolymer (BCP) directed self-assembly (DSA), which offers molecular-scale control over pattern formation and compatibility with existing lithographic processes, has emerged as a promising complementary nanopatterning technology for advanced semiconductor manufacturing. This review summarizes the microphase-separation mechanisms of DSA, major guiding strategies including graphoepitaxy and chemoepitaxy, and pattern-transfer techniques such as dry and wet etching and sequential infiltration synthesis (SIS). In terms of device applications, particular emphasis is placed on recent progress in DSA for Fin Field-Effect Transistor (FinFET) fin patterning, silicon nanostructures, high-density contact holes, memory devices, two-dimensional semiconductors, and Complementary Metal–Oxide–Semiconductor (CMOS) optoelectronic devices. Key challenges, including defect control, process-window optimization, pattern transfer, and wafer-scale manufacturing, are further discussed, together with future directions involving the integration of DSA with extreme ultraviolet (EUV) lithography, advanced etching, and data-driven process optimization. This review aims to outline the technological evolution of DSA from nanoscale self-assembly toward integration into advanced semiconductor manufacturing and to provide a reference for high-resolution patterning at advanced technology nodes.

title: Peptide Self‐Assembly: Insights From Functional Short Peptides, Amyloid‐β, and Gluten Peptides
abstract: ABSTRACT In this perspective, we discuss how short peptides can be programmed through sequence design, stereochemistry, terminal modification, and external stimuli to form diverse supramolecular architectures. We then examine how similar molecular principles underlie disease‐associated aggregation, focusing on early Aβ(1–42) assemblies in Alzheimer's disease and proteolysis‐resistant gluten peptide nanostructures in gluten‐related disorders. Attention is given to the detection, stabilization, and modulation of transient oligomeric species, which remain challenging but highly relevant to therapeutic and diagnostic targets. We further highlight how short functional peptides can be engineered to interfere with aggregation pathways in amyloid and nonamyloid aggregopathies, including diabetes‐related amyloids, α‐synuclein, and phenylalanine assemblies. Together, these examples illustrate the cross‐applicability of concepts from supramolecular materials chemistry to molecular pathology. This perspective emphasizes that understanding peptide self‐assembly at the molecular level is key to both exploiting and controlling its biological consequences.

title: Design and synthesis of responsive glycopolymers for biomedical and environmental applications
abstract: Abstract Glycopolymers are a unique class of synthetic polymers bearing pendant carbohydrate moieties and have emerged as an important class of functional materials owing to their biocompatibility, biodegradability, hydrophilicity, and ability to mimic the functions of natural glycans in biological systems. These inherent properties enable specific carbohydrate‐lectin interactions involving cellular recognition, signalling, and pathogen binding, providing intrinsic biological recognition and biocompatibility. The integration of responsive segments into glycopolymer architectures has led to the evolution of smart materials capable of undergoing reversible physicochemical changes in response to pH, temperature, redox, light, and other bio‐stimuli, thereby dynamically altering their conformation, self‐assembly, and binding affinity. These stimuli‐responsive features of glycopolymers have shown tremendous potential in a wide range of applications, including biomedicine, biosensing, diagnostics, drug delivery systems, water purification, dye removal, and hydrogen production. This review highlights the advances in synthetic methodologies, including controlled radical polymerization technique, surface‐grafting approaches, post‐polymerization modification, and ring‐opening polymerization with precise structural control, which have significantly broadened the scope of glycopolymer synthesis. These advances reinforce the potential of responsive glycopolymers as versatile and sustainable materials for advanced biomedical and environmental applications.

title: Innovative Electrochemical Synthesis of Portland Cement Precursor (Ca(OH)2) with Machine Learning-Enabled Predictive Insights
abstract: For long the manufacturing of calcium hydroxide, a major precursor of cement production, has relied heavily on the calcining of calcium carbonate, which not only costs much energy, but also releases a significant amount of carbon dioxide. To electrochemically synthesize calcium hydroxide is a high-potential substitution, as it utilizes the pH gradient to decarbonate limestone and generate calcium hydroxide, which can be carried out at room temperature. But creating a pH gradient with electrolysis of water requires a relatively high voltage, which could be energy-draining in manufacturing. Hence, here an innovative three-chamber electrolysis system based on hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) and hydrogen oxidation reaction (HOR) is proposed, which lowers the electrolysis voltage to ~1.7 V at 150 mA while achieving ~100% coulombic efficiency for CaCO3 dissolution. A regularized linear regression model and a multi-layer perceptron are also developed as methodological demonstrations to (i) analyze the influence of key factors, including current, electrolyte concentration, and gas flow rate, on the calcium hydroxide production rate of the system; and (ii) infer potential main constraint of the system. Ion migration behavior during electrolysis is studied, suggesting that the main constraint lies in the unwanted migration of Ca2+ and OH−. The possibility of further applying deep learning to optimize experimental parameters, recognize major restrictions from high-dimensional data, and predict test results is also discussed, with prediction reliability constrained by limited experimental samples. This work offers a conceptually promising decarbonized pathway for cement-precursor production and references for combining electrochemistry with machine learning.

title: Chiral Materials for the Recognition and Inhibition of Amyloid‐β Aggregation
abstract: Abnormal aggregation of amyloid-β (Aβ) peptides is a central pathological event in Alzheimer's disease (AD), closely associated with neurotoxicity and disease progression. The development of molecules or materials with high selectivity and affinity toward Aβ aggregates constitutes an essential component for the early diagnosis and intervention of AD. Aβ peptides, composed of homochiral amino acids, undergo intermolecular β-sheet assembly to form supramolecular chiral aggregates, providing a structural basis for chirality-sensitive recognition. Therefore, chiral materials have attracted significant attention in Aβ aggregates recognition and regulation. Previous reviews have examined different types of chiral materials for the inhibition of Aβ aggregation, including chiral small molecules, amino acids, peptides, and various chiral interfaces or nanomaterials. The present review organizes reported chiral materials according to three intervention strategies for modulating Aβ aggregation: conformation-locking, self-assembly-induced remodeling, and multifunctional intervention. We summarize representative materials in each category, along with the corresponding design principles and modulation performance toward Aβ aggregation. Current challenges and potential directions for the development of chiral therapeutics for AD are also discussed.

title: Computational model of developmental self-assembly of a cortical microcircuit
abstract: Cortical microcircuits emerge from local developmental interactions, yet large-scale computational models typically prescribe connectivity rather than explain its formation. Here we use BioDynaMo to simulate the self-assembly of ~70,000 cortical neurons from 1,200 progenitors in 3D physical space through migration, neurite growth and contact-based synapse formation. With one calibrated filling fraction per connection type, the locally formed synapses reproduce experimentally measured connectivity across 64 connection types (mean absolute error 0.0062) without prescribing individual connections. The grown spiking networks sustain stable, inhibition-dominated activity, and the same developmental rules, given different targets, generate both a canonical cortical microcircuit and a visual-cortex variant. Inverting the migration programme produces a reeler-like column whose aberrant connectivity destabilises network activity. Together, these findings provide a mechanistic link between local developmental processes and the emergence of cortical anatomy, connectivity and function.

title: Enhanced Surface Area of Mesoporous Alumina Fibers for Fluoride Removal
abstract: Mesoporous alumina fibers (MAFs) combine strong fluoride affinity with a readily recoverable fibrous form, but calcination-induced shrinkage and pore collapse can reduce the surface area available for adsorption. MAF and nine variants doped with alkali metals (Li, Na, and K), alkaline earth metals (Mg, Sr, and Ba), or rare earth metals (Y, La, and Ce) were prepared by CTAB-assisted electrospinning to evaluate how dopant selection affected post-calcination pore structure, BET surface area, and fluoride removal. Li, Na, and K doping mainly increased the pore volume and average pore diameter, whereas Mg, Sr, Ba, Y, La, and Ce doping increased the BET surface area and reduced the average pore diameter relative to MAF. Across the ten samples, fluoride removal efficiency was strongly and positively correlated with BET surface area (R2 = 0.9149, p < 0.001). MAF-Y exhibited the highest BET surface area (237.89 m2·g−1) and fluoride removal efficiency (68.00%). Its Langmuir-estimated maximum adsorption capacity was 51.49 mg·g−1 at 50 °C and pH 7. Overall, dopant selection effectively regulated the post-calcination pore structure of MAF. Y doping most effectively preserved the mesoporous structure, thereby increasing BET surface area and fluoride removal.

title: Mesoporous TiO2-500/FeOClfev Composites for Enhanced Photo-Fenton Degradation of Sulfamethoxazole
abstract: Developing photo-Fenton catalysts that efficiently couple photogenerated charge separation with Fe redox cycling is essential for improving water treatment. Here, a TiO2-500/FeOClfev heterojunction was constructed to combine interfacial charge transfer with H2O2-assisted oxidation. The optimized 1:1 composite removed approximately 90% of sulfamethoxazole (SMX) within 10 min under simulated solar irradiation, whereas TiO2-500 and FeOCl achieved only 12.7% and 13.2% removal, respectively, under otherwise identical conditions; the NaCl-assisted FeOClfev-0.15 component achieved 81.9% removal. Structural and spectroscopic analyses indicate intimate interfacial contact, extended visible-light absorption, and interfacial electronic interactions. Enhanced photocurrent and a reduced electrochemical impedance arc further suggest more efficient charge separation and transport. Scavenger and electron spin resonance experiments identify •O2− and h+ as the dominant reactive species, with •OH also contributing. A possible direct Z-scheme pathway and Fe-mediated H2O2 activation are proposed to explain the observed behavior. These results demonstrate that coupling TiO2-500 with NaCl-assisted FeOCl is a promising strategy for improving photo-Fenton catalysis for antibiotic abatement.

title: Segregated MWCNT Networks in XNBR via Interfacial Assembly for Enhanced Mechanical, Dielectric, and EMI Shielding Performance
abstract: ABSTRACT Segregated networks of carboxylated multiwalled carbon nanotubes (MWCNTRs) were developed in carboxylated acrylonitrile–butadiene rubber (XNBR) through latex‐stage processing. The composites exhibited a low electrical percolation threshold of approximately 0.05 vol% and an increase in dielectric constant from 23 for unfilled XNBR to approximately 7000 at 7 phr MWCNTR (100 Hz). At 0.3 phr, tensile strength and 300% modulus improved by approximately 65% and 32%, respectively. A maximum EMI shielding effectiveness of 5.3 dB was obtained in the X‐band (8–12 GHz). Microscopic observations and strain‐sweep measurements supported segregated network formation, while swelling studies indicated improved solvent resistance. These findings demonstrate that the segregated MWCNTR network contributes to enhanced electrical, dielectric, and mechanical properties, with moderate EMI shielding performance.
